title: Experiment Governance Ledger and Guardrail Integration (WIP)
body:
Summary:
This working doc captures a proposed lightweight ledger for cross-functional experiment governance plus a mapping pattern for integrating automated guardrails into the ledger lifecycle. The goal is to make sign-offs auditable at a feature/experiment level and to bind telemetry-derived guardrail events to explicit ledger states so we can automate partial rollbacks and runbooks where safe.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- We run cross-team canaries and A/B tests frequently; signal ownership and sign-off are fragmented (product, infra, SRE, safety, solutions).
- Manual sign-off is slow and inconsistent; automation exists in silos (alerts, feature flags, rollout console) but not tied to a single source-of-truth for the experiment state.
- When an automated guardrail fires, operators often lack context: which sign-offs were completed, what fallbacks are allowed, who to page.

Key objectives:
- Create a minimal experiment ledger that records required sign-offs, current state, risk budget consumption, and fallback permissions.
- Surface ledger state in the Redwood Console and expose it to guardrail automation (alerting, auto-scaling, flight toggles).
- Define deterministic mapping from telemetry/alert types -> ledger actions (e.g., 'safety-high' -> auto-fallback to baseline for 30m + page oncall).
- Preserve human-in-the-loop for escalations while enabling safe automated remediation.

Ledger (proposed fields, intentionally minimal):
- experiment_id: human-friendly id (e.g., AB-2024-148)
- title: string
- owning_product_team: string
- start_window: YYYY-MM-DD / time window
- target_cohorts: short list of cohort names (e.g., beta-users, us-east-1 mobile)
- risk_budget: numeric (units = error-rate-pct or SLI-weighted points)
- risk_consumed: numeric (updated by telemetry hooks)
- required_signoffs: list of roles (product, qa, infra, srel, trust)
- signoff_status: map role->(signed_by,timestamp,status) [note: for Drive doc we keep it as table view in console]
- fallback_policy: short code referencing runbook (e.g., FALLBACK-A: degrade to model-v1 + disable rerank)
- guardrail_bindings: list of guardrail rules (see below)
- current_state: draft | active | paused | rolled-back | completed
- last_action_log: append-only short strings

Operational flows (high-level):
1) Create ledger entry during experiment planning PR, populate required_signoffs.
2) Each sign-off is an explicit console action; signing requires a short rationale comment.
3) Once all mandatory sign-offs exist, experiment moves to 'active' and traffic is enabled per plan.
4) Telemetry runs in steady-state and posts risk_consumed updates to ledger via a read/write API.
5) Guardrail rules evaluate; when triggered they emit a ledger action (annotate + perform automated step per binding).

Guardrail binding pattern (example schema described in plain language):
- guardrail_id: short id (e.g., GR-001)
- trigger_condition: short english description + link to alert rule (e.g., "p95 latency increase > 250ms vs baseline for 3m")
- severity: low|medium|high
- precondition: ledger_state must be 'active' and fallback_policy allowed for automation
- automated_action: one of [scale-up, scale-down, route-to-backend, revert-model, reduce-cohort, pause-exposure, no-op] with arguments
- human_notification: slack channel + oncall role
- cooldown: seconds/minutes
- post_action_verification: simple check (e.g., latency returns within threshold in 10m)

Concrete examples to anchor thinking:
- GR-101 (safety-high): trigger = toxic-detect-rate > 1% over baseline for 10m; severity=high; automated_action = revert-to-baseline-model (FALLBACK-A) + pause-exposure; human_notification = #safety-oncall; cooldown = 30m; post_action_verification = monitor toxicity rate for 20m.
- GR-210 (latency-bump): trigger = p95 > 250ms for 2 consecutive 5m windows; severity=medium; automated_action = reduce_cohort_by_half; human_notification = #sre-ops; cooldown = 15m; verification = p95 below 220ms in 10m.

Sign-off flows & nuance:
- Not all signoffs need to be completed for 'soft' experiments (internal pilot). Ledger supports optional vs required flags.
- For high-risk experiments (sensitive customers / compliance scope) the ledger requires an escalation approver (senior PM + legal + security) and disables auto-remediation unless explicitly allowed.
- Signoffs should capture short rationale + test artifacts (links). Avoid large attachments in ledger; link to Confluence.

Integrations (where to wire things):
- Redwood Console: render ledger card in the experiment page (status, signoffs, risk_consumed graph, latest guardrail hits).
- Telemetry/Observability: an agent (small lambda) aggregates SLOs into a risk score and writes it to ledger via API.
- Guardrail automation service: subscribes to alerts and to ledger state; performs actions using rollout API / feature flag toggles.
- PagerDuty/Slack: configured per guardrail binding for immediate context.
- Audit logs: every ledger mutation goes to central audit store.

Operator play examples (short):
- Play A: Safety guardrail fires (GR-101). Automated revert is executed. Console shows ledger state changed to 'paused', last_action_log annotated. SRE runs verification script, if failure persists, Open Incident and escalate per Incident runbook.
- Play B: Noise spike in p95 latency; GR-210 reduces cohort by 50%. Product owner allowed to manually re-enable split; ledger records rationale.

Open questions & tradeoffs (we should resolve before implementation):
- Q1: Canonical risk budget unit: should we normalize across SLIs (latency, toxicity, error-rate) or keep separate buckets?  Tradeoff: normalized simplifies automation but can hide SLI-specific failure modes.
- Q2: Who holds the authority to enable full automation for a given experiment? Propose a role-level toggle (srel leads + product director signoff).
- Q3: How do we handle multiple overlapping experiments modifying the same surface? Need conflict resolution policy (priority, last-writer wins, or block if overlapping cohorts).
- Q4: How much of the ledger should be editable post-activation? Suggest only add notes; signoffs immutable after activation except by an 'editor' role with audit trail.

Implementation immediate next steps (MVP-ish):
- [ ] Finalize ledger field set (short meeting with SRE + Safety + Product) -- owner: Riley (this doc).
- [ ] Prototype ledger UI card in console (static mock) -- owner: Product-Console (Maya).
- [ ] Build telemetry -> risk score job (PoC query + webhook) -- owner: Observability (Ethan).
- [ ] Wire guardrail service to accept ledger state and test with one GR (latency) in staging -- owner: Serving Runtime / SRE.
- [ ] Draft runbooks for two automated guardrails (safety-high & latency-bump) and rehearse a dry-run.

Notes to reviewers / how to use this doc:
- This is intentionally concise — I want feedback on the ledger surface and the automated guardrail binding pattern.
- If you are an owner listed in the linked_artifacts, please add a short comment below with objections or missing fields.
- Mark your preferred option for Q1 (risk budget normalization) with a short rationale.

References & helpful links:
- Confluence (governance primer): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/EX-3421-experiment-governance
- Example alert rules: https://observability.redwood.ai/alerts/GR-210-latency
- Feature flag API (rollout): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts#api

Revision history (simple):
- 2024-11-15: created (initial sketch)
- 2024-12-04: added guardrail binding examples and signoff nuance (Maya)
- 2025-01-10: updated next steps and owners after sync with SRE (Ethan)

Quick TODO for sync meeting (prep):
- Bring a short sample experiment to demo the ledger (preferably one with a nontrivial fallback).
- Prepare two example alert traces (safety + latency) for GH staging.
- Decide on one cohort overlap rule to test for the prototype.

-- end of draft --
